title: I'm researching if LLMs can be synthetic players for games consumer research
author: sifujordo
selftext:
Hi everyone,

I am a contributor at [Naavik](http://www.naavik.co) and am conducting independent research for an upcoming article (to be published for free) on the efficacy of using LLMs for consumer research in the gaming industry.

Recent studies (like [this one on ArXiv](https://arxiv.org/html/2510.08338v1)) have successfully used LLMs to reproduce human purchase intent for consumer products. I’m looking to see if that same methodology works for games. If it works, it could provide us with a fast, low-cost way to get early signals on game concepts.

Part of the method is collecting human data to calibrate and validate the LLM results. I’m looking for participants to take an anonymous **3-5 minute survey** on 5 early-stage mobile game concepts

**Survey Link**: [https://forms.gle/sAtbnoVMixuKKysf9](https://forms.gle/sAtbnoVMixuKKysf9)

I'll be sure to share a summary of the findings back with this community once the analysis is complete! Thank you.

comments.author: sifujordo
comments.body: Just posting an update for anyone that was interested. Unfortunately there haven't been enough response to be statistically significant so I haven't used this days in my article.

comments.author: Kiryoko
comments.body:
Hey, I'm a Naavik fan and long-term viewer!

I love your podcasts, I just wanted to say hi and that I appreciate what you guys are doing :)

On the topic of the post and the survey, I've been making bots and automate games since I was a teenager.

I played a lot of MMORPGs and PBBGs throughout my life.

Of course, the natural next step for me was to try and break one using LLMs :D

So, yeah, I hooked up an LLM to a custom API to control the actions of a specific browser game (that I won't name :P) and honestly it's soooo cool and it works wonders!

Of course, it depends on the nature of the game, however this can be done and you can tell the LLM to impersonate a specific player persona, and it will try and follow it pretty cleanly.

Also, I've been building my own browser MMO game, and I'm been trying to fit this into the testing phase, but honestly I'm just running my game sim with economy and game rules for balance at scale to optimize parameters for now... because LLMs are kinda slow and expensive for this task.

But the outlook is promising.

Cheers!

replies.author: sifujordo
replies.body: Hey, I appreciate this note. What you're doing seems pretty interesting too!
